text:
Leah (CS): Quick thread  - Corbin Health procurement wants a short SLA packet for their security/compliance folder. They asked for: MUP definition, p50/p95/p99 latency targets, credit calc with a worked example, onboarding timeline, and notes about model warm-up and multi-region behavior. Renewal touchpoint in ~5 weeks. Can @Marco (SRE) and @Nina (Solutions) confirm numbers so I can draft?
Marco (SRE): Hosted baseline: monthly uptime percentage (MUP) = 99.9%. Typical latency targets: p50=100ms, p95=350ms, p99=900ms (p99 reflects tail behavior on heavy long-context requests). Dedicated commitment = 99.95% MUP. Note: first-hour rollout/model-swap may see p95/p99 spikes due to KV cache and JIT; call this out as "warm-up window."
Nina (Solutions): Agree. Suggested plain-language line: "Latency SLOs are measured on steady-state production traffic; transient spikes during initial deployments, model swaps, or cold KV cache warming are expected and documented in onboarding guidance."
Leah (CS): Credits: procurement requested an explicit formula + a worked example they can paste into the contract.
Marco (SRE): Use our customer-friendly formula with a cap: ```credit = round(min(0.3, max(0, (SLO_target - observed_MUP) / SLO_target)) * committed_monthly_fee, 2)``` Cap = 30% of committed monthly spend.
Nina (Solutions): Worked example for clarity: "Committed = $12,000/mo; Target MUP = 99.9%; Observed MUP = 99.6% => shortfall = 0.3% => credit = min(30%, 0.003/0.999) * $12,000 ≈ $36. Credits applied as invoice credit on next billing cycle (not cash)."
Owen (AE): Corbin has bursty inference at day-end batch times. Recommend we include optional mitigations they can purchase: Reserved concurrency (dedicated pool), Scheduled pre-warm window (1hr), and Autoscale ceiling tuning. Also note Dedicated provisioning lead time = 2-3 weeks.
Leah (CS): Action list: (1) Marco - paste final monitoring query/dashboard snapshot for MUP and a short note on per-region SLO behavior; (2) Nina - draft the one-pager + simple 2-row table (Hosted vs Dedicated) with p50/p95/p99, credit cap, add-ons, lead times; (3) Owen - prepare add-on pricing bullets and renewal owner. I'll send to procurement by Thursday EOD.
Marco (SRE): Metric name confirmed: "monthly uptime percentage (MUP)". PromQL example (30d window): `sum_over_time(up{service="inference-api"}[30d]) / (30*24*3600)` . Dashboard snapshot will be posted here: https://redwood.metrics/corbin/mup-snapshot once Nina finalizes text. Small legal note: multi-region customers have per-region SLOs; we report aggregated availability but credits apply per-region unless contract states otherwise.
Nina (Solutions): Drafting now. Onboarding timeline (short): Day 0: kickoff + API keys; Day 1-2: integration tests + smoke; Day 3-4: canary + perf tuning; Day 7: scale to steady-state. Optional accelerated 3-day path with pre-warm slot (needs coordination). I'll include a one-line FAQ: "What causes short-term latency spikes?" answer: warm-up, model swaps, traffic bursts, and long-context requests.
SLA-Bot: Reminder set — ping thread members 2024-06-05T15:00:00Z to finalize one-pager.
Leah (CS): Thanks all. Please drop final snippets into https://redwood.docs/corbin/sla-packet-draft by Wednesday 12:00 PT. I'll consolidate and attach to procurement packet. :thumbsup:
